lens: all three in turn: learning-scientist, examiner, learner-advocate
coverage: Read module.json in full (nodes S1.start to END, traps, objectives, claims, cards, report). Walked the first two probes of every segment (S1 to S8) with their trap feedback, retries, hints and fast lanes; sampled the deeper branches (S2.d1-d4, S4.dp1, S6.d_*, S6.pal/bt_q2, S7.d1-d4, S7.d3). Spot-checked the target of every next in the sampled nodes. Not every node was read individually.
gate_notes: No gate failure found. No node asks the learner to type; no run-time AI. Graph: no dead ends or missing targets found in the nodes read. I had no execution tool, so the graph check is a read-through, not a programmatic validation.

segments.reason: Strong blue-baby hook; probes come before teaching. Weak points: S1.q1b and S1.q3b are same-form retests, and S1.q3b restates the cue from the stem (the answer is nearly given).

Best mechanism ladder: four rungs with a trap and a causal repair on each. Weak points: S2.s2 has only two options, S2.s3 stem gives the key away ('day after day'), and S2.d4 has a dominated option ('All series agree on exactly 5 to 7').
Pink-Tet vignette, predict-the-murmur before listening, and the spell murmur is traced via K20. Weak points: S3.case1r repeats S3.case1 in the same form, and S3.ret keys by length.

S4.f3 is telegraphed: the only hedged option is the key, and the stem says 'reading the wording of the source'. S4.t2 explains CT before the S4.t3 probe asks it, so there is no retrieval. S4.start puts two left-sided distractors against one right-sided key.

Worked case A/B then a learner-chosen case C; ordering and lever probes; trap feedback gives the reason. Weak points: S5.c1b's key is the only drug-free option; S5.m1_expl is generic for both TR8 and TR11 and never names the heart-failure model; S5.d1's key is the longest option.

Good 'What it misses' trap feedback and clean repair pathway. But S6.open has a dominated distractor ('Deferred until school age'), S6.open and S6.bt are repeated almost verbatim in S7.m7a and S7.m7b, and S6.k1/k2 are fine but the sure-notes add little.

Classmate-correction format is a good PYQ drill, but many items repeat earlier probes in the same form (S3.not to S7.m4, S3.case1 to S7.m3b, S6.open to S7.m7a, S6.bt to S7.m7b, S2.s3 to S8.g1b). S7.d2's distractor 'TOF stays pink until the neonatal period ends' maps to TR7 but no TR7 holder would pick it. Typos: 'Right. one surgical review', 'one surgical review do not'.

Cold checks are mostly verbatim copies of earlier probes: S8.g2 = S4.f1, S8.g2b ~ S4.start, S8.g3 = S4.t4, S8.g4 ~ S5.d1, S8.g5 ~ S6.r1. A learner who got the earlier item right can repeat it, so the 'cold' evidence the report relies on cannot separate recall from memory of the key. Otherwise the take-home is clean.

best_parts: S2.s1 to S2.asm (four-rung ladder): each rung has a trap, and S2.s3_t1 names the 'flat list' model; S2.s3_ok then shows the chain in a device line.

S3.spell_t8a / S3.spell_ex / S3.not and S3.ret: predict the murmur change before listening, trace the falling RVOT flow via K20, and re-test the same idea in a vignette (S3.ret) with a distinct TR11 distractor.

S5.c1_t to S5.c1b: a wrong first step routes to a re-test in another form (pick two) rather than straight to the answer; S5.c2_t9 names the pulmonary-side lever as tempting and then rebuilds SVR vs PVR.
flaws: S4.f3 (key 'Films may classically show a boot; it is not guaranteed'): the only hedged option, while the other two are absolute. The stem's 'Reading the wording of the source' gives the key away (DP1).

S8.g2, S8.g2b, S8.g3, S8.g4, S8.g5 (cold 'Gate' checks): near-verbatim copies of S4.f1, S4.start, S4.t4, S5.d1 and S6.r1 with the same keys and distractors. Cold evidence is compromised (DP11, R2 re-test in another form).
S4.t2 (explain): tells CT as the morphology test one node before S4.t3 asks it. Ask-before-tell broken; the probe is a recall check of the line just read.
further_flaws: S6.open: 'Deferred until school age' is dominated (no learner who knows TOF repair timing would pick it). S7.m7a is the same stem and options as S6.open.
S7.d2 'TOF stays pink until the neonatal period ends' is mapped to TR7, but TR7 is 'every TOF is blue from birth'. Nobody holding TR7 picks this; it diagnoses nothing.

S2.start 'Right ventricular hypertrophy' is mapped TR14 while its feedback (S2.start_t14) refutes the TR2 model (RVH as a defect). S2.s3 'Overriding aorta' is mapped TR2; trap-map P05 says TR1. Label mismatches break the trap-to-feedback link.
S5.c1b key 'Knee-chest and oxygen' is the only option with no drug name; the trap options all name drugs (findable by form, DP1). S5.d1 key is the longest option.
S5.m1b 'Heart failure from left ventricular dysfunction' (TR11) routes to S5.m1_expl, which explains only the murmur (TR8) and says 'both readings are tempting', which is wrong for this option.
S2.d4 'All series agree on exactly 5 to 7' is an absolute-word distractor that nobody holding TR17 would pick (dominated).
S2.s2 has two options only; S2.s3 stem 'consequence of the others... day after day' gives the key.
S4.start: two of three distractors start 'Left'; the key is the only option without 'left' (findable by form).

Voice and meta: 'the source' / 'this source' / 'Imaging teaching' appear on main-path feedback (S4.f3_hint, S4.f3, S6.a_endo, S6.a_hint, S2.d1_t1) and read as citation-talk to a learner. Typos: S7.d3_ok 'Right. one surgical review', S7.d3_t1 'one surgical review do not'.

Schema: several nodes use sure_note: null (S7.d2_t1, S7.d2_t2, S7.d3_t1, S7.d3_t2, S7.d4_t1, S7.d4_t2, S7.m8 not), and S7.d1_t1's sure_note carries a 'flag' key that the other sure_notes lack. Check the renderer.
trap_coverage_check: Every TR1 to TR22 appears on at least one main-path probe; TR16, TR17 and TR22 are on main path only in S6.k1 and S7.m6/S7.m8 (TR16 only in deeper S7.d4 and S2.d1-d2). Unverified claims (K7, K17, K18, K33, K36, K38, K40, K41, K51 to K58, K71, K75, K78, K79 partly) appear only in deeper or flagged nodes that I read.
objective_coverage: Core O1 to O10 are on the main path and survive the fast-lane skips (S2.start_ok to S2.s3, S3.case1_ok to S3.safe, S4.ecg_why_ok to S4.f1, S4.t0_ok to S4.t3, S8.g2_ok to S8.g3). O11 and O12 are on the main path through S7.m6 and S7.m7a/S7.d2 (deeper only for the numbers).
merge_ideas: Keep the S2 four-rung ladder and S3 spell-murmur prediction; replace the cold S8 gates with new vignettes (new stems, new distractors) so the report can credit unaided recall.
Fix S4.f3 by giving the two absolute distractors a hedge of their own ('may' on all three, or none) and drop the 'reading the wording of the source' cue.
Give S5.m1_expl a separate heart-failure branch for TR11 (as S5.b1_t11 already does for fluids), and drop the 'both readings' phrasing.
sim_reports: No sim/*.report.json files could be opened at workshop/paediatrics/tetralogy-of-fallot/sim/ (the directory exists, but the expected file names did not resolve). R9 is therefore judged from report.json and the path design alone.
R9_report_judgement: report.json is detailed and well aimed: objective-level secure/shaky/gap with the matching card, trap-level avoided/fell_recovered/fell_open with the repair named, calibration and hint-use patterns. Weakness: it reports on the cold S8 gates, which repeat earlier items, so 'secure' on O6, O7 and O9 may reflect memory of keys rather than recall. Also the 'strong' headline promises 'mostly right first time' without saying which items were answered by key recall.
